title: p0161
universal_lens: The source establishes a structural duality: offensive dimensionality (run/pass balance) vs. defensive strength induces a state-dependent success kernel P(success|strong_defense, field_position) = 1/3 * σ(field_position), where σ is a sigmoidal risk-aversion operator. This creates a non-separable manifold where single-dimension offenses collapse to measure-zero victory sets.
gsi_mapping: GSI Bayesian update: prior P(win|pass_only) ≈ 0 from historical cases; likelihood L(data|strong_defense) = Binomial(n, p=1/3); posterior concentrates on multi-dimensional offenses. Conformal prediction sets for play-calling exclude pure-pass regions in own half with coverage 1-α, α=0.67, calibrated by the 2:1 odds.
gse_mapping: GSE state-transition: state s = (field_position, defensive_strength, offensive_dimension). Action a ∈ {run, pass}. Transition kernel T(s'|s,a) has absorbing loss states when a=pass in own half against strong defense. Value iteration yields optimal policy π*(s) = pass only when field_position > threshold ∧ offensive_dimension ≥ 2.

primitives.name: Forward Pass Success Probability Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: Given a strong defense, the chances are two to one against the success of the forward pass.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P: dimensionless probability [0,1]; D: defensive strength categorical {weak, strong}; success/failure: binary outcome {0,1}
primitives.assumptions: Independent Bernoulli trials per pass attempt; defense strength stationary during drive; no quarterback/weather covariates.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Collapses when D=weak (p→0.5+), or when offensive dimensionality ≥2 (play-action, run-pass option) breaking conditional independence.

layer2.mapping: GSI: likelihood kernel for Bayesian play-calling posterior. GSE: transition probability T(success|s, a=pass) in MDP. Isomorphic to Bernoulli bandit with known bias 2:1 against.
layer2.telemetry: Empirical pass completion rate vs. defensive EPA allowed; calibration plot of predicted vs. observed success in own half.

primitives.name: Field Position Risk-Aversion Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: It can be readily understood that the offense, in its own half of the field, is unwilling to take this chance of losing the ball.
primitives.latex: R(x) = \mathbb{I}[x \le 50] \cdot \lambda \cdot \frac{2}{3}, \quad x \in [0,100] \text{ yards from own goal line}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: R: dimensionless risk cost [0,1]; x: field position in yards [0,100]; λ: loss-aversion coefficient dimensionless >1; 50: midfield boundary yards
primitives.assumptions: Turnover cost scales with field position; own half defined as x ≤ 50; risk aversion monotonic in turnover consequence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Vanishes when x > 50 (opponent half) or when trailing late-game (λ → 0). Breaks if turnover probability ≠ 2/3 (e.g., screen passes).

layer2.mapping: GSI: conformal risk score for play-calling exclusion sets. GSE: state-dependent cost function C(s,a) in Bellman equation. Isomorphic to prospect theory value function with kink at midfield.
layer2.telemetry: Pass rate by field position bin; turnover rate on passes in own half vs. opponent half; win probability added (WPA) of pass vs. run in own territory.

primitives.name: Offensive Dimensionality Necessity Condition
primitives.verbatim_quote: 134 AMERICAN FOOTBALL experience, cite cases of teams unusually skillful in the pass which were unable to gain victories because the offense was limited to skillful passing alone.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: V: victory probability dimensionless [0,1]; dim(𝒪): cardinality of offensive play-type set dimensionless integer; 𝒪: offensive scheme space
primitives.assumptions: Victory requires sustained drives; defense adapts to single-dimension offense; dimensionality measured by distinct play-type concepts.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if defense has exploitable structural weakness (e.g., no pass rush) allowing dim(𝒪)=1 to succeed. Breaks in extreme weather forcing dim(𝒪)=1.

layer2.mapping: GSI: prior support constraint — posterior mass zero on dim(𝒪)=1 schemes. GSE: action space cardinality requirement for ergodic policy. Isomorphic to rank condition in linear control: controllability requires rank(B) ≥ 2.
layer2.telemetry: Win rate by offensive play-type diversity (Shannon entropy of play calls); defensive EPA vs. single-dimension offenses; playoff success of dim(𝒪)=1 teams.

primitives.name: Pass Impunity Field Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: Indeed, it has been found that the forward pass cannot be used generally and with impunity on all parts of the field against a The Attack by Passing A Downfield Pass strong defense.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P: dimensionless probability; x: field position yards [0,100]; k: steepness parameter yards⁻¹; σ: logistic sigmoid dimensionless
primitives.assumptions: Impunity means success probability > 0.5; field position modulates base 1/3 rate; strong defense uniform across field.
primitives.breakdown_regime: σ→1 when x≫50 (red zone) or k→0 (defense weak). Breaks if defense strength varies by zone (e.g., bend-don't-break).

layer2.mapping: GSI: spatially-varying likelihood for hierarchical Bayesian model. GSE: state-dependent transition kernel T(s'|s,a=pass,x). Isomorphic to inhomogeneous Poisson process with rate λ(x).
layer2.telemetry: Pass success rate by 10-yard field position bins against top-quartile defenses; logistic regression fit of success ~ field_position; AIC comparison vs. constant model.

reasoning_traces.think:
The source text provides three empirical anchors: (1) historical failure of pass-only offenses (dim(𝒪)=1 → V=0), (2) 2:1 odds against pass success vs. strong defense (p=1/3), (3) field-position-dependent risk aversion in own half. These form a coupled system: the base kernel p=1/3 is modulated by field position via sigmoid σ(x-50), creating a spatially inhomogeneous success probability. The dimensionality requirement emerges as a topological constraint: the victory manifold V>0 has codimension 1 in offensive scheme space, requiring at least two linearly independent play vectors to span. The risk operator R(x) = λ·(2/3)·𝕀[x≤50] acts as a barrier potential in the GSE Bellman equation, making pass actions in own half suboptimal unless λ→0 (desperation). Failure modes: when defense is weak (p→0.5), the kernel loses discriminative power; when dim(𝒪)≥2, play-action breaks the conditional independence assumption by coupling run/pass likelihoods; in late-game trailing scenarios, λ→0 eliminates the risk barrier. The 2:1 odds are not betting lines but empirical frequencies from 1930s football, implying a binomial process with n≈large, p=1/3.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The defense knows the offense's dimensionality: if dim(𝒪)=1 (pass-only), defense allocates 100% resources to pass coverage, driving p→0. The offense knows the defense knows, creating a signaling game where run establishment (dim(𝒪)≥2) is a costly signal to shift defensive resource allocation. The field-position risk aversion reflects the offense's belief that turnover in own half has asymmetric cost (λ>1) due to opponent scoring probability.
